correctness.rationale: The Legendre generating function and its derivative give the full Poisson kernel in the stated normalization. With q=cos(z/N)+i sin(z/N)cos(φ), parity and the Laplace integral express each omitted term as the integral of (2n+1)(−rq)^n. Because |q|≤1 and r<1, the sum can be taken inside the integral. The tail divided by (−r)^(N+1) is the average of q^(N+1) times [(2N+3)/(1+rq)−2rq/(1+rq)^2]. For fixed z, q^(N+1) tends uniformly to exp(iz cos(φ)), while the bracket divided by N tends uniformly to one. The normalized integral is therefore J₀(z). With δ=1−r_N(c), Nδ²→0 and N²r_N(c)^(N+1)/log N→e^(−c); the full kernel is δ/4·(1+o(1)) since the denominator tends to 8. Subtracting the tail yields the stated sign and prefactor for both parities. The series for J₀(4) has partial sum −1/3 at k=4, followed by a negative alternating remainder of decreasing magnitudes. Negativity for each fixed c below the respective threshold implies R_N<r_N(c), and taking c upward yields the liminf with the stated inequality direction. At r=1−β log N/N, the full-kernel to Nr^(N+1) ratio is O(log N·N^(β−2)), proving strict negativity at z=4 along even N for 0<β<2. These are obstructions only. The frozen numerical script was read, not run; the rational alternating-sum bound is in the proof, not the numerical script.
